intervention_label: FANCM-RMI interaction inhibitors (cell-active cyclic peptides) for ALT-positive tumours
target_feature_label: ATRX loss / alternative lengthening of telomeres (untested)
mechanism: FANCM uses its translocase activity and its grip on the BLM-TOP3A-RMI complex to hold telomeric replication stress in ALT cells below the level that kills them. Take FANCM away and ALT telomeres run away into fork collapse, telomere dysfunction and death, while telomerase-positive cells are largely unbothered. Cyclic peptides that sit in the FANCM pocket on RMI1/2 do this pharmacologically.
rationale: ATRX loss and ALT are common in uterine leiomyosarcoma, and the obvious ALT vulnerability - ATR inhibition - did not survive replication, which this case file already records. FANCM is the one ALT dependency with a better replication record: two groups published it independently in the same issue of Nature Communications in 2019, on top of an earlier PNAS study from a third group. Nothing about this patient's telomere biology has been measured, so the idea is contingent on ATRX sequencing or a C-circle assay coming back consistent with ALT.
novelty: No FANCM- or RMI-directed agent exists beyond academic cell-penetrating peptides, and FANCM appears nowhere in this case's trials, clinical-evidence or preclinical-evidence files.

key_manuscripts.finding: FANCM depletion drove break-induced telomere synthesis and ALT biomarkers upward, and blocking FANCM-BTR complex formation was selectively toxic to ALT cancer cells. The effect needed FANCM's translocase activity and its BTR contact, not the Fanconi core complex.

Independent report, same issue: depleting FANCM in ALT cells caused telomere dysfunction, arrested proliferation and killed them, and co-depleting BLM or overexpressing RNaseH1 rescued the phenotype. That places telomeric R-loops and unrestrained BLM at the centre of the mechanism.
Earlier work from a third group placing FANCM, BRCA1 and BLM together in resolving replication stress at ALT telomeres. It is the prior that the two 2019 papers built on.

First validated chemical inhibitors of FANCM-RMI, cyclic peptides from mRNA display binding RMI1/2 at KD 2-10 nM and disrupting the interaction at IC50 54-104 nM. Confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation in osteosarcoma lysates.
Conjugating the peptides to a cell-penetrating carrier produced antiproliferative activity in ALT-positive osteosarcoma lines. This is the first time the target has been engaged inside a cell.

Telomere-biology metrics, proteomics, CRISPR dependency and drug-sensitivity data across 976 cancer cell lines, nominating ALT-associated molecular vulnerabilities. Also shows telomere maintenance is not the clean binary the field has assumed, which matters for how an ALT-selective agent would be matched to patients.

developability: Chemical matter is a nanomolar cyclic peptide bolted to a cell-penetrating carrier, active in culture and nowhere else. No in-vivo pharmacokinetics, no tolerability data, no IND. A tractable small molecule or a stapled-peptide successor would have to come first.
risks: ALT and ATRX status in this patient are unmeasured, so the selection biomarker for the whole idea is missing
FANCM also restrains replication stress away from telomeres; systemic inhibition could destabilise normal proliferating tissue
All cellular activity to date is in osteosarcoma lines, with no leiomyosarcoma model tested
The ATR precedent in ALT shows how badly an ALT-selectivity claim can fail on isogenic re-testing
caveats: Do not read this across from the ATR story; the reason FANCM is worth carrying at all is that its replication record is better, and that claim would still need testing in an ALT-positive uLMS model.

intervention_label: SUV39H2 inhibitor OTS186935 combined with a PARP inhibitor
mechanism: SUV39H2 methylates H3K9 and helps recruit phosphorylated H2AX to double-strand breaks. Inhibiting it with OTS186935 blunts gamma-H2AX accumulation and degrades break repair, which is the state in which PARP inhibition becomes lethal rather than merely cytostatic.
rationale: This is one of the few synthetic-lethality papers run in uterine leiomyosarcoma itself rather than borrowed from another histology. SUV39H2 was higher in uLMS tissue than in normal myometrium or leiomyoma, and the combination outperformed either agent in a uLMS xenograft. The PARP-inhibitor half is already covered upstream in this case; the SUV39H2 half is not, and it offers a way to create the repair deficit rather than waiting to find one.
novelty: OTS186935 is an academic tool compound with no registered trial in any indication, and SUV39H2 appears in none of the upstream files for this case.

key_manuscripts.finding: OTS186935 cut viability in SK-LMS-1 and SK-UT-1, reduced gamma-H2AX by immunofluorescence and ChIP-seq, and combined with olaparib gave a combination index of 0.88 in SK-UT-1 with greater effect in subcutaneous uLMS xenografts. The authors themselves call for validation before any clinical read.

model_systems: uLMS cell lines SK-LMS-1 and SK-UT-1
subcutaneous uLMS xenograft in nude mice
uLMS vs myometrium vs leiomyoma tissue IHC
developability: OTS186935 is a probe, not a drug candidate: no published tolerability, no formulation work, no sponsor. The PARP-inhibitor partner is off the shelf, so the whole gap sits on the SUV39H2 side.
risks: One laboratory, one paper, and the synergy showed in only one of two cell lines
A combination index of 0.88 is barely inside the synergy range and could move with assay conditions
The olaparib contribution may depend on HR status, which is untested in this patient
No toxicology whatsoever for SUV39H2 inhibition, and H3K9 methylation has broad roles outside repair
caveats: SK-UT-1 and SK-LMS-1 are the standard uLMS lines but both carry long-standing identity and provenance questions, which slightly discounts even a well-matched result.

intervention_label: CD70-directed antibody-drug conjugate (anti-CD70-MMAF) in uterine leiomyosarcoma
mechanism: Membrane proteomics of uLMS lines against normal myometrium picked out CD70 as a differentially expressed surface antigen. An anti-CD70 antibody carrying a monomethyl auristatin F derivative internalises on antigen binding and delivers a mitotic poison to the cell that expressed it.
rationale: The antigen work upstream in this case is B7-H3 and FAP, both of which come with either an antigen-density problem or on-target stromal toxicity. CD70 came out of an unbiased uLMS membrane-proteomics screen and was overexpressed in 19 of 21 uLMS specimens, with activity in both a cell-line xenograft and a patient-derived xenograft. For a tumour with almost no recurrent activating driver, a surface antigen is one of the few handles that does not require a mutation to exist.
novelty: No CD70-directed agent appears in this case's trials.jsonl and no CD70 program exists in sarcoma; the conjugate in the source paper is an academic construct.

key_manuscripts.journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
key_manuscripts.finding: CD70 was overexpressed in 19 of 21 uLMS specimens, and the anti-CD70-MMAF conjugate killed SK-LMS-1 at an IC50 of 0.120 nM with no effect on CD70-negative cells. Tumour volume fell 54.5% in the SK-LMS-1 xenograft and 84.7% in a patient-derived xenograft.
RNA-sequencing survey of antibody- and CAR-targetable surface antigens across soft-tissue sarcoma subtypes, providing an independent expression frame for antigen selection in this histology.

model_systems: uLMS cell lines SK-UT-1, SK-LMS-1, SKN
developability: The conjugate itself is academic, but CD70 binders have been built for other diseases, so the antibody engineering is not the bottleneck. What is missing is anyone willing to run a sarcoma program, plus a CD70 IHC assay to select patients.
risks: CD70 is expressed on activated T cells, B cells and dendritic cells, so immune-compartment toxicity is a real question
Only one of three uLMS lines was CD70-positive by western blot despite 90% positivity in tissue - that discordance is unexplained and matters for patient selection
MMAF is a non-cleavable payload with no bystander effect, which is a poor match for a heterogeneously expressed antigen
CD70 status is unmeasured in this patient and is not on the case's biomarker survey
caveats: CD70-directed molecules have reached patients in haematology and renal cancer, so the class is not naive; the uLMS-specific construct and indication are what sit at the preclinical stage.

intervention_label: PI3K/mTOR inhibition plus PD-1 blockade, selected by pS6-high uLMS
mechanism: PI3K/mTOR overactivation, read out as high phospho-S6, tracks with lymphocyte-depleted immune landscapes in leiomyosarcoma. Inhibiting the pathway repolarises macrophages away from the pro-tumour phenotype and raises antigen presentation on dendritic and tumour cells, which converts a PD-1-refractory tumour into one where PD-1 blockade has something to work with.
rationale: The single-cell picture of metastatic uLMS in this case file is an M2-dominant myeloid compartment with exhausted CD8 T cells, and pembrolizumab monotherapy is already known not to work in this histology. This is the only published intervention that remodelled that specific microenvironment in a humanized uLMS patient-derived xenograft and produced partial or complete responses when paired with anti-PD-1, where anti-PD-1 alone did nothing. It also brings a selection biomarker, pS6, that is not on this case's biomarker survey and could be added to a single IHC slide.
novelty: No registered trial pairs a PI3K/mTOR inhibitor with PD-1 blockade in uterine leiomyosarcoma, and pS6-based selection appears in none of the upstream files; pembrolizumab monotherapy is what trial_screener covered.

key_manuscripts.finding: In an ICB-resistant humanized uLMS PDX, PI3K/mTOR inhibition repolarised macrophages and raised antigen presentation, and the combination with anti-PD-1 produced partial or complete responses while single-agent anti-PD-1 produced none. Serial single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing showed clonal expansion of a cytotoxic CD8 population.
Single-cell profiling of patient-derived uterine leiomyosarcoma describing the suppressive niche this candidate is aimed at. It is the phenotype the PI3K/mTOR result claims to reverse.

developability: Both halves exist as approved or late-stage agents in other diseases, so the missing piece is a sponsor and a pS6-selected sarcoma protocol rather than chemistry. That also means the boundary here is the combination and the biomarker, not the drugs.
risks: Both components are individually clinical-stage; only the pairing and the pS6 selection are preclinical, which makes the novelty claim narrower than for the other rows here
Humanized PDX immunology is reconstituted, not native, and overstates how faithfully a mouse can model a human myeloid compartment
pS6 is unmeasured in this patient
Pneumonitis risk from PD-1 blockade and hyperglycaemia from PI3K/mTOR inhibition are a poor fit for someone with bilateral pulmonary disease living at 8,500 ft
caveats: The PDX responses were in a single model system from a single group. Nothing here has been tested alongside trabectedin, which is already depleting the same macrophage compartment.

intervention_label: Anti-MARCO antibody reprogramming of suppressive tumour-associated macrophages
mechanism: MARCO is a scavenger receptor marking a suppressive macrophage subset. An antibody against it, working through the inhibitory Fc receptor FcgammaRIIB, flips those macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory state instead of depleting them, and in parallel licenses NK-cell killing of the tumour.
rationale: The uLMS microenvironment described in this case is macrophage-heavy and T-cell-exhausted, and trabectedin already depletes monocytes and TAMs, so a myeloid-directed partner has an obvious combination logic. MARCO antibodies reprogram rather than delete, which is a different lever from trabectedin's and could in principle be additive rather than redundant. The evidence is entirely in carcinoma and melanoma models, so the read across to sarcoma is an assumption, not a finding.
novelty: No anti-MARCO antibody has entered clinical development in any indication, and MARCO appears nowhere in this case's upstream files.

key_manuscripts.finding: An anti-MARCO monoclonal antibody reprogrammed suppressive TAMs to a pro-inflammatory phenotype and slowed breast, colon and melanoma models, with the effect dependent on FcgammaRIIB. It also improved checkpoint-inhibitor efficacy.
Targeting MARCO on immunosuppressive lung-tumour macrophages blocked regulatory T cells and restored cytotoxic lymphocyte function. Independent group, independent tumour type.
Anti-MARCO antibody treatment activated NK-cell killing of tumour cells, adding a second effector arm to the macrophage-reprogramming mechanism.
The uLMS single-cell data describing the M2-skewed macrophage compartment that would have to carry MARCO for this to be relevant. Whether it does is untested.

model_systems: syngeneic breast, colon and melanoma mouse models
developability: Research-grade antibodies only, with no humanized clinical candidate and no reported tolerability package. A humanization and Fc-engineering effort would come before anything else, and the FcgammaRIIB dependence complicates that engineering.
risks: MARCO is also expressed on alveolar macrophages; a myeloid-directed antibody in someone with bilateral pulmonary metastases and reduced reserve at altitude carries a specific lung-toxicity concern
MARCO expression in uterine leiomyosarcoma has not been measured by anyone
Trabectedin is already depleting the same compartment, so the two could be redundant rather than complementary
No sarcoma model has been tested, and sarcoma myeloid biology is not interchangeable with carcinoma myeloid biology
caveats: Every efficacy result comes from two laboratory groups working in carcinoma and melanoma. The case for sarcoma rests on phenotype similarity, which is a weak argument on its own.

intervention_label: Ferroptosis blockade as anthracycline cardioprotection (ferrostatin-1, MitoTEMPO, GPX4 induction)
target_feature_label: anthracycline exposure in a 30-39-year-old at altitude
mechanism: Doxorubicin degrades haem through Nrf2-driven Hmox1 induction, releasing free iron that accumulates in cardiomyocyte mitochondria and drives lipid peroxidation. Blocking that with ferrostatin-1, chelating mitochondrial iron, scavenging with MitoTEMPO or raising GPX4 prevents the cardiomyocyte death that dexrazoxane only partly prevents.
rationale: She is under 40, systemic-therapy naive, and about to start doxorubicin with a maintenance phase, which makes late cardiac injury a decades-long problem rather than a treatment-window one. Two independent groups showed in mice that ferroptosis, not apoptosis or necroptosis, is the dominant mode of doxorubicin cardiomyocyte death, with genetic and pharmacologic confirmation in both. One of them compared ferrostatin-1 directly against dexrazoxane and found it did better, which is the closest thing to a benchmark this field has. This case file already carries hypoxic preconditioning as a cardioprotection mechanism; the ferroptosis route is a different lever and has more replication behind it.
novelty: No ferroptosis inhibitor has a clinical-grade formulation or an oncology cardioprotection program; dexrazoxane is the only agent with human data and works by a different mechanism.

key_manuscripts.finding: In apoptosis- and necroptosis-defective mice, doxorubicin still killed cardiomyocytes by ferroptosis, and ferrostatin-1 reduced cardiomyopathy more than dexrazoxane did. Blocking Hmox1 with zinc protoporphyrin IX or scavenging with MitoTEMPO gave the same protection, tying the effect to haem-derived free iron in mitochondria.

Independent replication: doxorubicin downregulated GPX4 and drove mitochondrial lipid peroxidation, cardiac injury worsened in GPX4-heterozygous mice and improved in GPX4 transgenics. Ferrostatin-1 plus a caspase inhibitor fully prevented cardiomyocyte death in culture.
Pharmacological activation of GPX4 improved doxorubicin cardiomyopathy in mice, which converts the genetic GPX4 result into a druggable direction.

developability: Ferrostatin-1 and MitoTEMPO are laboratory reagents with no human formulation, and the GPX4-activator chemistry is early. Someone would need a clinical-grade radical-trapping antioxidant before this could be a protocol, and the first such protocol would have to be a cardiology-endpoint study, not a sarcoma one.
risks: The unanswered question is whether the same protection extends to the tumour; if ferroptosis contributes to doxorubicin's antitumour effect, this could blunt the therapy it is meant to enable
No ferroptosis inhibitor exists in clinical-grade form, so nothing here is orderable
Chronic hypoxic adaptation at 8,500 ft shifts iron handling and haemoglobin, and no model has looked at anthracycline ferroptosis under those conditions
Dexrazoxane already has human data and would not be displaced by a mouse result
caveats: This is a supportive-care hypothesis, not an antitumour one, and it should not compete for attention with the disease-directed candidates. Baseline echocardiography is the actionable step today.

intervention_label: IL1R2 decoy-receptor blockade to release antitumour neutrophils in sarcoma
mechanism: IL1R2 is a decoy receptor that soaks up IL-1 and damps its signalling. Removing it in mice raises IL-1-driven emergency granulopoiesis and floods the tumour with neutrophils whose transcriptional programme shifts away from pro-tumour functions toward activation and maturation.
rationale: The pulmonary lesions here were read as unusually infiltrative and possibly inflammatory, and the field's default assumption - that tumour inflammation is uniformly pro-tumour - is what this work contradicts. The effect was selective for sarcoma across four tumour types tested, which is unusual and makes it worth carrying for this histology specifically. An IL1R2-deficiency gene signature also correlated with better outcome in human sarcoma, which is the only human anchor the idea has.
novelty: No IL1R2-directed therapeutic exists in any development programme; the published work is genetic deficiency in mice, and nothing in the case's upstream files touches the IL-1 axis.

key_manuscripts.finding: IL1R2 deficiency reduced sarcoma growth selectively - not colorectal, not lung - with massive neutrophil infiltration, neutrophilia and reprogramming away from pro-tumour transcriptional programmes. Neutrophil depletion abolished the tumour control, and an IL1R2-deficiency signature tracked with better outcomes in patients with sarcoma.

model_systems: transplantable and chemically induced mouse sarcoma, primary and metastatic
colorectal and lung mouse models as negative comparators
developability: There is no molecule. Blocking a decoy receptor to increase signalling of its ligand is also an unusual pharmacological ask, and it is not obvious an antibody would reproduce a germline knockout. A tool antibody and a conditional-deletion timing experiment would both come before anything else.
risks: Genetic deficiency from birth is not the same as blocking a receptor in an adult with established metastases
One laboratory, one paper, no replication
Recruiting neutrophils into lungs already carrying bilateral infiltrative disease could worsen symptoms before it does anything useful
The broader literature mostly reports neutrophils as pro-metastatic in lung, so this cuts against the prevailing direction and needs more than one result
caveats: The human data is a correlative signature, not a treated cohort. Nothing here has been tested in leiomyosarcoma specifically.

intervention_label: PLOD2 / lysyl hydroxylase 2 inhibition to reverse hypoxic collagen cross-linking in sarcoma
target_feature_label: hypoxia-driven collagen matrix and immune exclusion
mechanism: Hypoxia drives HIF-1alpha to induce PLOD2, which hydroxylates collagen lysines and organises the matrix into the aligned, stiff configuration that supports sarcoma dissemination. Its collagen VI product also pushes CD8 T cells toward dysfunction, so suppressing PLOD2 acts on both the metastatic scaffold and the immune exclusion at once.
rationale: The hypoxia-PLOD2 mechanism is already in this case's preclinical evidence as biology; what is not there is any intervention against it. A 2024 preprint took the step from mechanism to treatment, showing that suppressing Plod2 slowed sarcoma growth in an immune-competent host and improved anti-PD-1 efficacy. That combination of a metastasis-promoting matrix and an immune-cold tumour is a reasonable description of what is happening in these lungs, and hypoxia is a plausible driver in someone living at 8,500 ft, though nobody has studied that interaction.
novelty: No selective LH2/PLOD2 inhibitor exists in clinical development; the only pharmacology reported is minoxidil acting as a non-selective transcriptional suppressor, and no oncology programme has been built on it.

key_manuscripts.finding: Genetic and pharmacologic suppression of Plod2, the latter with the pan-Plod transcriptional inhibitor minoxidil, reduced undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma growth in a syngeneic immune-competent transplant system and improved anti-Pd1 efficacy. Preprint, not peer reviewed at the time of writing.

key_manuscripts.journal: Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics
key_manuscripts.finding: A direct cautionary note that minoxidil does not usefully inhibit lysyl hydroxylases in vivo in developing mouse lung. It is the reason the pharmacology in this row is treated as a concept rather than a repurposing plan.

model_systems: syngeneic undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma mouse model
developability: There is no selective LH2 inhibitor. Minoxidil suppresses PLOD transcription broadly rather than inhibiting the enzyme, and a published note argues it cannot be used as an LH2 tool in vivo. A genuine inhibitor would have to be discovered before this is testable.
risks: Systemic minoxidil causes fluid retention, tachycardia and pericardial effusion, which is a poor pairing with an anthracycline
Loosening collagen cross-links could plausibly aid dissemination rather than restrain it; the direction of effect is not settled
All efficacy data is in undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, not leiomyosarcoma
The primary source is an unrefereed preprint
caveats: The underlying hypoxia-PLOD2 mechanism paper is already logged in this case's preclinical evidence; what is new here is only the attempt to intervene on it.

intervention_label: RAD52 inhibition (6-OH-dopa, RPA:RAD52 interaction inhibitors) in BRCA2-deleted tumours
mechanism: RAD52 runs a backup single-strand annealing route that BRCA-deficient cells lean on once homologous recombination is gone. Small molecules that collapse RAD52's undecamer rings into dimers, or block its contact with RPA, remove that backup and are selectively lethal in BRCA-deficient cells.
rationale: The HRD subset of uterine leiomyosarcoma arises largely through BRCA2 homozygous deletion, which means no protein at all rather than a hypomorphic point mutant, and that is the cleanest genetic background for a RAD52 dependency. It is also a mechanism distinct from PARP inhibition, which is the route already covered upstream and the one that reversion mutations and restored HR eventually defeat. Everything here is contingent on HR testing that has not been done.
novelty: No RAD52 inhibitor has entered clinical development in any indication; the compounds are academic chemical probes and RAD52 appears nowhere upstream in this case.

key_manuscripts.finding: 6-hydroxy-DL-dopa allosterically transformed RAD52 rings into dimers, abolishing the ssDNA binding channel, and selectively inhibited proliferation of BRCA-deficient cancer cells including patient leukaemia samples. Other double-strand-break repair pathways were largely unaffected.
Structure-based selection identified a second, chemically distinct RAD52 inhibitor, giving the target more than one chemotype.
Inhibitors of the RPA:RAD52 protein-protein interface selectively killed homologous-recombination-deficient cancer cell lines, an orthogonal way into the same dependency.

developability: All three chemotypes are probes. 6-OH-dopa in particular is a redox-active catechol with the promiscuity that implies, and none has in-vivo efficacy or a tolerability package. A real medicinal-chemistry campaign has not happened.
risks: HR status and BRCA2 copy number are untested in this patient, so the selection biomarker does not exist yet
6-OH-dopa's redox activity makes clean target attribution hard and any cellular selectivity suspect
No leiomyosarcoma model has been tested
If HRD is confirmed, PARP inhibition is far better developed and would come first; this only becomes interesting after that fails
caveats: Nothing here has progressed past cell culture in a decade of published work, which is itself informative about how hard the target is.

intervention_label: Collateral-lethality mapping of the 13q homozygous-deletion footprint in uLMS
mechanism: Homozygous deletions rarely take only the gene they are named for. When a 13q event removes BRCA2 at 13q13.1, and often RB1 at 13q14 with it, the neighbouring passenger genes go too. Where one of those passengers is a redundant member of an essential gene family, or a core essential gene left at reduced dosage, the surviving paralogue or the residual copy becomes a tumour-specific dependency that normal cells do not share.
rationale: uLMS is defined by loss rather than gain, and 13q is one of the recurrent losses, which makes it the natural place to look for a dependency created by the deletion itself rather than by a driver. The CYCLOPS framework showed that partial copy loss of core essential genes produces exactly this kind of liability, and the collateral-lethality precedents from other tumour types show it can be drugged. Nobody has run this analysis for the leiomyosarcoma 13q footprint, and the first step is a copy-number map rather than a molecule - which this patient does not yet have, since no sequencing has been done.
novelty: No compound, no programme and no published analysis of the uLMS 13q deletion footprint exists; this is a research direction rather than a candidate agent.

key_manuscripts.finding: Integrating copy number with genome-wide RNAi identified 56 CYCLOPS genes whose suppression selectively killed cells with partial copy loss of that gene, enriched for spliceosome, proteasome and ribosome components. PSMC2 was worked out in detail as the proof of principle.

key_manuscripts.journal: Journal of Experimental & Clinical Cancer Research
key_manuscripts.finding: Establishes that the HR-deficient subset of uterine leiomyosarcoma arises through BRCA2 homozygous deletion with COSMIC signature 3 and high genome-wide LOH. That deletion is the event whose footprint this idea proposes to map.
Prospective clinical sequencing of uterine sarcomas describing the recurrent copy-number losses, including 13q, that define the genomic shape of this disease.

developability: There is nothing to develop yet. The work is computational and functional-genomic first: segment the 13q event at high resolution across uLMS cohorts, intersect with dependency data, and only then ask whether any surviving paralogue is druggable. Years, and possibly no molecule at the end.
risks: Entirely untested in leiomyosarcoma; the reasoning is transposed from pancreatic and glioma precedents
Deletion boundaries differ between patients, so any vulnerability found would be per-tumour rather than per-disease and would need this patient's own copy-number data
CYCLOPS dependencies are usually dosage effects on core essential genes, which makes the therapeutic window narrow by construction
No sequencing has been performed on this patient, so even the first analytical step is blocked
caveats: Logged as a direction so it is visible rather than as anything actionable. Its only near-term implication is an argument for copy-number-aware sequencing rather than a panel that reports mutations alone.

intervention_label: Arginine deprivation combined with BCL-XL blockade in ASS1-deficient sarcoma
mechanism: Sarcomas that silence argininosuccinate synthetase 1 cannot make their own arginine and depend on the extracellular supply. Removing that supply arrests them but does not kill them, because BCL-XL binds BAX and BAK and holds the intrinsic apoptosis pathway shut. Releasing BAX and BAK with a BCL-XL inhibitor converts the arrest into cell death.
rationale: ASS1 loss is recurrent in sarcoma and is not on this case's biomarker survey, so it is an unmeasured vulnerability sitting inside the stated molecular gap. Arginine deprivation on its own has underperformed clinically, and this work offers a mechanistic account of why rather than another attempt at the same thing. The combination has not been tested in patients in any tumour type.
novelty: ADI-PEG20 monotherapy is clinical-stage and is not the candidate here; the pairing with BH3-mimetic BCL-XL blockade is preclinical only and appears in no registered trial.

key_manuscripts.finding: Arginine deprivation reduced CDK2 activity and arrested ASS1-deficient cells without killing them, because BCL-XL was bound to BAX and BAK. Inhibiting BCL-XL released the intrinsic apoptosis pathway and increased cell death, with synergy in vitro and efficacy modelled in vivo.

Earlier work from the same group pairing arginine deprivation with chloroquine to kill ASS1-deficient sarcomas, establishing that the arrest needs a second hit to become lethal. Different second hit, same underlying logic.

model_systems: ASS1-deficient sarcoma and carcinoma cell lines
developability: Both components exist as clinical agents in other diseases, so the missing piece is a trial rather than chemistry - but BCL-XL inhibition carries platelet toxicity that has held the class back for a decade, and that is the real obstacle.
risks: BCL-XL inhibition causes dose-limiting thrombocytopenia, which stacks badly on doxorubicin and trabectedin myelosuppression
ASS1 status is unmeasured in this patient and is not on the biomarker survey
Arginine deprivation monotherapy has already disappointed in sarcoma, so the combination inherits a discouraging clinical prior
One group has generated most of this evidence
caveats: The boundary here is thinner than for the other rows: the individual agents have been in patients, and only the combination and the sarcoma context are preclinical.

intervention_label: WEE1 inhibition selected by ATRX loss
mechanism: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in isogenic ATRX-null cells nominated WEE1 among 58 selective dependencies; WEE1 inhibition then drove DNA-damage-induced apoptosis in ATRX-deficient lines and xenografts.
rationale: ATRX loss is common in uLMS and this is a well-constructed isogenic screen, so the biology is worth recording even though the agent is not mine to carry.
exclusion_reason: WEE1 inhibitors including adavosertib and azenosertib are enrolling patients across multiple indications, which puts the intervention in trial_screener's territory rather than this horizon scan.

key_manuscripts.finding: WEE1 emerged from a genome-wide synthetic-lethal screen in ATRX-null hepatocellular carcinoma cells, and AZD1775 inhibited ATRX-deficient lines, xenografts and ATRX-mutant primary glioma cells.

intervention_label: KIF18A inhibition in chromosomally unstable, aneuploid tumours
mechanism: KIF18A is dispensable in near-diploid cells but required for viable mitosis in tumours carrying chromosomal instability and whole-genome doubling, which makes inhibition selectively lethal in aneuploid backgrounds.
rationale: uLMS is a copy-number-driven, heavily aneuploid disease, so ploidy-selective lethality is an obvious fit for the histology and worth logging even though the agents have moved past this tier.
exclusion_reason: Several KIF18A inhibitors are already in first-in-human phase 1 studies, so the class sits with trial_screener rather than in a pre-clinical horizon scan.

key_manuscripts.finding: The KIF18A inhibitor ATX020 induced mitotic arrest and DNA damage selectively in chromosomally unstable high-grade serous ovarian cancer cells.

intervention_label: LP-184, an acylfulvene alkylating agent for HRD tumours
mechanism: An acylfulvene prodrug activated by PTGR1 that generates DNA lesions repaired through nucleotide excision repair, with activity concentrated in homologous-recombination-deficient backgrounds.
rationale: HRD in uLMS is a real subset and an alkylator with an HRD-selective profile would sit near the olaparib plus temozolomide logic already in this case.
exclusion_reason: LP-184 has entered first-in-human phase 1 testing, so it is a clinical-stage agent and belongs to trial_screener.

key_manuscripts.finding: LP-184 showed activity across solid tumour models with homologous recombination deficiency, with sensitivity tracking HRD status.

intervention_label: Polymerase theta (POLQ) inhibition in HR-deficient tumours
mechanism: POLQ drives microhomology-mediated end joining, the repair route HR-deficient cells fall back on. Blocking it is synthetic lethal with HR loss and is also active where PARP-inhibitor resistance has emerged.
rationale: BRCA2-deleted uLMS is exactly the background where POLQ inhibition was designed to work, and it would be a natural successor to the olaparib route already logged in this case.
exclusion_reason: POLQ inhibitors including ART4215 are enrolling patients, so the mechanism has passed out of the preclinical tier and into trial_screener's scope.

key_manuscripts.finding: Simultaneous targeting of POLQ with either PARP1 or RAD52 produced dual synthetic lethality in HR-deficient leukaemia cells, mapping how the backup repair routes interlock.

intervention_label: TREM2 blockade to remodel the suppressive myeloid landscape
mechanism: TREM2 marks a lipid-associated macrophage state that accumulates in tumours; antibody blockade shifts the myeloid compartment and improves anti-PD-1 activity in mouse models.
rationale: The M2-dominant uLMS microenvironment is the phenotype TREM2 blockade was built for, and it would have been a natural pairing with trabectedin's monocyte depletion.
exclusion_reason: PY314, a TREM2-directed antibody, has completed a phase 1b study with pembrolizumab, so the mechanism is clinical-stage and sits with trial_screener.

key_manuscripts.finding: TREM2 modulation remodelled the tumour myeloid landscape and enhanced anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in mouse models.
Phase 1b of the anti-TREM2 antibody PY314 with pembrolizumab in advanced renal cell carcinoma, which is what places this mechanism in the clinical tier.

intervention_label: Neutrophil extracellular trap degradation (DNase I / dornase alfa repurposing) in the pulmonary metastatic niche
mechanism: Tumour-induced neutrophil extracellular traps build a DNA scaffold in the lung that supports metastatic seeding and shields tumour cells from cytotoxic lymphocytes; DNase I degrades the scaffold.
rationale: An infiltrative, possibly inflammatory pulmonary pattern is the kind of phenotype NET biology has been invoked to explain, and dornase alfa is an approved inhaled enzyme, so the repurposing route would be short.
exclusion_reason: The mechanism has not been connected to sarcoma at all - no leiomyosarcoma or sarcoma model links NETs to the infiltrative pulmonary phenotype - so it does not yet act on the stated feature, and logging it as a candidate would overstate a purely carcinoma-derived idea.

key_manuscripts.finding: Cancer cells induced neutrophil extracellular DNA traps that supported metastasis, and DNase-coated nanoparticles reduced lung metastasis in breast cancer models.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition selected by ALT status
mechanism: The original claim was that ALT cells, having uncoupled TERRA regulation through ATRX loss, depend on ATR to survive telomeric replication stress, making them acutely sensitive to ATR inhibition.
rationale: Re-examined because ATRX loss and ALT are the most likely molecular features of this tumour, and this was the field's default ALT vulnerability for several years.
exclusion_reason: Already logged in this case's preclinical_evidence.jsonl including both failed replications, and ATR inhibitors are clinical-stage besides. Carried here only so the audit trail shows the ALT branch was re-checked rather than assumed closed.
